title: Good CONCURRENTLY index build — correct non-blocking pattern outside transaction
migration_snippet:
-- V7__add_search_index.sql
-- flyway:executeInTransaction=false
SET statement_timeout = '0';  -- CONCURRENTLY can take time, don't timeout
SET lock_timeout = '10s';     -- but don't wait forever for initial lock
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_search ON orders USING gin (search_vector);

-- IF NOT EXISTS matches on NAME only: a pre-existing idx_orders_search on different
-- columns would survive untouched. Verify what actually exists AND fail on a mismatch --
-- a bare SELECT reads the definition but cannot act on it.
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_indexes
     WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND indexname = 'idx_orders_search'
       AND indexdef LIKE '%gin (search_vector)%'
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'idx_orders_search exists but is not the intended index: %',
      (SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexname = 'idx_orders_search');
  END IF;
END $$;
expected_feedback: No violations. Correct CONCURRENTLY usage: (1) flyway directive to run outside transaction, (2) statement_timeout disabled for long-running build, (3) lock_timeout set for initial lock acquisition, (4) IF NOT EXISTS for idempotency, (5) appropriate GIN index type for tsvector. The pg_indexes.indexdef check after the build is what closes the IF NOT EXISTS name-only hole, and it has to be able to FAIL: a bare SELECT of indexdef proves the definition was read, never that it was verified. Without a RAISE EXCEPTION on mismatch, an existing index on other columns silently survives and the intended index is never created.
